Anomalous

/uh-NOM-uh-lus/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Anomalous means departing from what is standard, normal, or expected.

The night-shift technician flagged an anomalous reading from the water sensor, a spike of pressure that matched nothing in the plant's normal cycle.

Worked Example

While cataloguing the greenhouse, the botany students found one anomalous orchid blooming in deep shade, even though every guidebook said the species needs six hours of direct sun. They set up a camera to figure out how it was surviving.

The orchid breaks the normal, expected pattern for its species, which is exactly what anomalous describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

irregular: Irregular describes the uneven shape or timing of a whole series or schedule, as in an irregular heartbeat or irregular attendance. Anomalous points at a single result or reading that clashes with what the established pattern predicts, and so demands an explanation.

abnormal: Abnormal measures something against a general or healthy standard, and it usually passes judgment: abnormal levels are worrying. Anomalous is the cooler, more technical word — it says only that a result fails to fit the established pattern, without judging it good or bad.

inconsistent: Inconsistent means failing to agree with the rest of the data or behavior; the pieces do not line up with one another. An anomalous result goes further: it clashes with the whole established pattern so sharply that it cannot simply be explained away.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

normal: matching the usual standard

predictable: behaving just as expected

Where it sits · how sharply it defies expectation — unusual → anomalous → freakish

unusual vs. anomalous: An unusual result is merely uncommon, while an anomalous one clashes with the established pattern and demands an explanation.

freakish vs. anomalous: An anomalous reading breaks the expected pattern, but a freakish one is so wildly out of range that it seems almost unbelievable.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — an-

Prefix — an-: not, without (Greek)

Root — omal

Root — omal: even, uniform, from Greek homalos, 'level,' itself from homos, 'same'

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of, having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Anomalous is built from Greek an-, 'not,' plus homalos, 'even or uniform,' which itself comes from homos, 'same.' Something anomalous is literally 'not uniform,' the one piece of data or behavior that refuses to lie level with everything around it.

Use the root in a new word: homogenize

Use the root in a new word: homogenize: The dairy homogenizes its milk so the cream stays evenly blended throughout, drawing on the same Greek root homos, 'same,' that hides inside anomalous.

Word Choice

formal, common in science and data analysis

Anomalous is the adjective to reach for when a result, reading, or behavior fails to fit the established pattern, especially in scientific and statistical writing. The related noun anomaly names the irregular thing itself, while anomalous describes it.
